state.project: Miu World: a voxel learning game for Vietnamese grade-2 children (web, iPad Gen 10), built 100% by AI. The owner's single wish: truly lively so children never get bored.
state.owner_feedback: The child complains about standing in one place too long during quests. This batch spreads every quest over at least 4 places (at most 2 steps in a row at one place) and adds about 140 quest characters (each in at most 2 quests). The owner adds: 'the maps may be made bigger to fit the quests and the new NPCs; let Jev decide.'
facts: Both playable maps are 192x48x192 blocks (made 4x bigger today). Performance re-measured today on them: 60 FPS average on an emulated iPad and phone, at most 108 draw calls of 150, first area 1.85 MB of an 8 MB budget, load 2.1-2.7 s.
Only one quest's places and characters are in the world at a time; quests of the same zone reuse its ground.

School: each of the 7 topic zones is about 40x40 to 42x60 blocks inside a walled campus; each quest stays in its topic's zone (an earlier decision). Forest: the whole map outside the chapter-1 corner is open to quest places, with 6 meadows.

Today the places of one quest stand only 2-6 blocks apart, so even a quest that moves between places barely makes the child walk. The placer can try wider gaps first (for example 14, then 10, then 7 blocks).
Growing a map means regenerating it, re-placing every quest, re-shooting the review pages and re-measuring performance; a bigger map loads more chunk data.

map_size.instructions: Should the maps grow for this batch?

criteria.grow_where_crowded: Keep 192x192 first and widen the gaps between a quest's places (14, 10, 7 blocks tried in order); after placing, enlarge a map (school zones or forest) only if its quests' places cannot keep at least 10 blocks apart, then re-measure performance.
criteria.keep_size: Keep both maps at 192x192 whatever happens; accept narrower gaps where a zone is crowded.
criteria.grow_both_now: Grow both maps to 256x256 now (78% more ground), give every zone and meadow more room, regenerate and re-measure.
